key_insight: Adapting which LLM to query next—and when to stop—while accounting for congestion can reduce total classification costs compared with fixed-order cascades.
engineering_relevance: Shared LLM classification services can balance error penalties, query fees, and waiting costs by routing jobs using observed outputs and congestion prices.
method: Represent adaptive routing policies as mixtures of decision trees and derive holding costs for specified queueing models.
Optimize model loads with a convex formulation and use congestion prices in a Bayesian routing-and-stopping dynamic program.
Compute policies through column generation with explicit optimality-gap and cascade-depth bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments separating the benefits of adaptive model selection and congestion-aware design, but gives no datasets or quantitative results.
watch_item: Exact holding-cost results rely on specified queueing assumptions; deployments with different service dynamics need validation.
paper_title: Congestion-Aware Adaptive Routing for LLM Classification
